Refuted on (c) and (d): the comparison is one-sided. The lead removes the same held poses from the score with its own stop label. I measured this with tools/alignment_skeptic_why_labels.py (new; models unchanged; frozen protocol; fit gaps 13.0 / 12.5 reproduce both fast claims). Output: docs/alignment/remeasure/conecut-knee-knuckle-3r_skeptic_why_held.json. The lead labels all of 752, 897, 965 (and 392, 530) 'slide': its knee loop has no solution in its window [ang_min, 180 - ang_min], which is the physical knee stop of CLAUDE.md (5), checked by skin-normal-3r-pin-knee.py line 147. The lead's held count is slide 32, the same as its verify _v_held_frozen.json why.slide 32. Its held per-pose dump has ev false at all five, so in the lead's 23.45 these poses also cost reach only. Fold is 260 on both rows. Charging the 3 upper-stop poses as contacts here (22.72) and not there compares a penalised row with an unpenalised lead. Like for like, the held edge at these poses is 0, so the 1.07 held edge does not rest on the relabel. For the wearer the pose is blocked by a hard stop in both designs, a dowel here and the knee window there, not by metal in the arm. A stop there costs the wearer nothing that the lead does not also cost. Correction to the count: J3MIN also cuts held 392 and 530 (q3' -112.49 / -114.49). They pass the parts check (part_clear 1.31 mm, equal to the taken-pose minimum 1.3146 in deep.coord_spans.clear) and would be contacts at -1.11 / -9.68 mm (verify c3_stopped). So a one-sided T6 count is 5 held poses (+0.56), but the lead's slide covers all 5.
